welcome.title: Good to have you here.
welcome.hint: We'll ask you a few short questions. After that you'll know where you're at home in CoFoundery.

name.title: What should we call you?
name.hint: This is how you'll appear to other people here.

plan.title: What are you here to do?
plan.hint: This decides which areas open up for you. There's no wrong answer – and none that locks you in.

focus.title: Where's your focus?
focus.hint: A rough direction is enough. It gets more specific on its own.

intention.title: What would you like to do here first?
intention.hint: This sets the context for what you see here — and you can change it any time.

avatar.title: Want to add a picture?
avatar.hint: Entirely optional. You can do it later any time.

next.title: These are your areas
next.hint: You'll find them in the bar at the top from now on.

onboarding.welcomeText: It takes a minute, and you can change everything later.
onboarding.focusOtherPlaceholder: If you like, describe your focus more specifically here
onboarding.avatarSkipHint: It is completely fine to skip this for now.
onboarding.nonDiagnosticHint: CoFoundery Align is not a personality test. It helps you make collaboration clearer and more resilient early.
onboarding.stepsLeft: {count, plural, =0 {Last step} =1 {One more step} other {# more steps}}

founder.title: I want to found a company
founder.description: You're building something, or you firmly intend to – alone or with a team.

advisor.title: I support founders
advisor.description: You bring experience and work with teams in an advisory role.

both.title: Both
both.description: You're founding yourself and passing on what you've learned at the same time.

connect.title: Just meet people for now
connect.description: You want to see who's around here before committing to anything.

onboarding.planChangeable: Nothing is final: as a founder or advisor you can change this any time in your profile.

align.name: Align
align.text: Here you work out how you work and decide – and how well that fits with someone else. Not a personality test, but a basis for honest conversations.
align.textAdvisor: Here you see what the people you support have shared with you — their answers and where they differ. You do not fill anything in here yourself.

find.name: Find
find.text: Here you look for people you could found with. You say what you're looking for and what you bring – and see who fits.

connect.name: Connect
connect.text: Here you meet the network: people with what they offer and need, real problems from other people's days – and everything business ideas grow out of.

onboarding.areasLater: You can add the other areas whenever you like – in your profile, with one checkbox.
onboarding.planChangeableConnect: And if you decide to found something later, we'll open up Align and Find – just drop us a line.
onboarding.areasLaterConnect: Align and Find are open to you whenever you want – just get in touch and we'll unlock them.
onboarding.nonDiagnosticHintAdvisor: CoFoundery Align is not a personality test. It helps the teams you support make their collaboration clearer and more robust, early on.

avatar.title: Avatar
avatar.help: Optional. You can set it now or change it later in the dashboard.

edit.rolesHelp: The core role for your onboarding is already set. Here you can activate additional modes.
edit.advisorRoleHelp: Use CoFoundery to support founder teams as an advisor as well.
edit.founderRoleHelp: Use CoFoundery for your own founder profile, matching, and alignment.

Suche.label: Searching
Suche.description: You want to see early who collaboration could really work with.

Partner-Match.label: Partner match
Partner-Match.description: You want to clarify fit and differences in a specific co-founder constellation.

Selbsttest.label: Self-check
Selbsttest.description: You first want to understand your own profile and way of working more clearly.

Begleiten.label: Supporting teams
Begleiten.description: You work with founders in an advisory role and want to make their collaboration clearer.

Teamklaerung.label: Working with one team
Teamklaerung.description: You are supporting a specific team and want to surface differences and expectations.

founderProfile.intro: Everything you have worked out about yourself in one place: who you are, how you work and what you bring. This page is visible only to you. To pass it on, print it or save it as a PDF.

base.title: Who you are
base.empty: Nothing about you yet. One sentence about yourself and your focus areas make the difference between a profile and a readout.

capability.title: What you bring
capability.intro: Per area: how often you have applied it and how you would see responsibility for it. The situations you told in the interview are deliberately not shown here — they stay on your profile page.
capability.evidenceCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 piece of evidence} other {# pieces of evidence}}

missingReport.title: Your self-report is still missing
missingReport.text: The questionnaire shows how you work and what matters to you. Without it the profile is missing half — the half people ask about most.

missingCapability.title: Your capabilities are still missing
missingCapability.text: In the interview you tell real situations, and the areas with evidence come out of them. That is the part that makes this profile more than a list of keywords.

direction.title: What matters to you
direction.intro: From the direction conversation — only what you confirmed yourself. The stories behind it stay with you.

missingDirection.title: Your direction is still missing
missingDirection.text: Six questions about real situations show which themes and changes keep pulling you in. That is the part a CV cannot give.

strengths.title: How you work
strengths.intro: Ways of working from situations you told — with your own assessment and what you assume others would say.
strengths.subtitle: Working styles from your situations

coverage.title: What you have talked about
coverage.intro: One bar per family, made of its individual areas — shaded by how far you have answered for each. These are counts, not a rating: a pale bar means the area has not come up yet, not that something is missing.
coverage.basis: This map counts your own entries. It says what the interview covered — not what you are capable of.
coverage.rolesIntro: Areas that cannot be bought in — and that you want to own. After Günter Faltin's component model: whatever exists as a finished service needs nobody on the team. What is listed here does.
coverage.rolesNone: None so far. Either the areas you discussed are buyable, or you have not yet said whether you want to own them.
coverage.rolesOpen: {count, plural, =1 {One more area belongs on the team, but you do not want to own it} other {# more areas belong on the team, but you do not want to own them}} — that is not a gap in you, it is an open question in the venture.
coverage.rolesCaveat: This does not say how good you are at it. It says you want to take it on, and that it cannot be bought in.
